## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design distributed rate limiting across DCs with per-tenant controls and edge enforcement. Highlights trade-offs: Redis replication latency, Lua script atomics, and failure handling.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant Redis namespaces and Lua-based token bucket
- Traefik middleware edge enforcement
- Docker Config for dynamic per-tenant rates and operators
- Cross-DC replication, failover, TLS/mTLS

## Code Example
```lua
-- Redis Lua script (atomic token bucket)
local bucket = KEYS[1]
local now = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local rate = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local capacity = tonumber(ARGV[3])
local tokens = tonumber(redis.call('GET', bucket) or capacity)
tokens = math.min(capacity, tokens + rate)
if tokens >= 1 then
  redis.call('SET', bucket, tokens-1, 'PX', 60000)
  return 1
else
  return 0
end
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test bursty traffic and DC failover under load?
- How would you handle Redis unavailability or clock skew between DCs?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests TLS termination, Docker Secrets, Configs, and per-tenant routing in a simple stack.

- TLS termination with Docker Secrets
- Docker Configs for dynamic Nginx config
- Multi-tenant server blocks in Nginx
- Simple health checks and verification

## Code Example
```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - '443:443'
    secrets:
      - tls_api
    configs:
      - source: tenant_nginx_conf
        target: /etc/nginx/conf.d/tenant.conf
    networks:
      - web
  api:
    image: myapi:latest
    networks:
      - web
configs:
  tenant_nginx_conf:
    external: true
secrets:
  tls_api:
    external: true
networks:
  web:
    driver: overlay
```

```nginx
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  server_name tenantA.api.local;
  ssl_certificate /run/secrets/tls_api/cert.pem;
  ssl_certificate_key /run/secrets/tls_api/key.pem;

}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to add observability to a Docker-based multi‑DC setup: tracing, TLS, and simple integration between app, edge, and backend collector. It’s beginner-friendly yet practical for real-world deployments.

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry instrumentation and OTLP exporter
- OpenTelemetry Collector and Jaeger backend
- TLS edge proxy (Nginx) and service TLS wiring
- Docker-Compose service wiring and basic config validation

## Code Example
```javascript
// docker-compose.yml (skeleton)
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    image: your-api-image
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
  nginx:
    image: nginx:stable
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest
    command: ["--config=/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./otel-config.yaml:/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml:ro
  jaeger:
    image: jaegertracing/all-in-one
    ports:
      - "16686:16686"
      - "4317:4317"
```

```python
# Example: instrument Flask app (conceptual)
from flask import Flask
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.flask import FlaskInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.http import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import SERVICE_NAME, Resource
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor

app = Flask(__name__)
FlaskInstrumentor().instrument_app(app)
trace_provider = TracerProvider(resource=Resource.create({SERVICE_NAME: 'api-service'}))
trace_provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint='http://otel-collector:4317/v1/traces')))
app.run()
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adjust sampling or add baggage propagation across DCs?
- How would you validate traces when altering infrastructure (edge restarts, collector restarts)?

```nginx
# nginx.conf
http {
  map $http_x_tenant $limit {
    default 1r/s;
    'tenantA' 5r/s;
    'tenantB' 2r/s;
  }
  limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=per_tenant:10m rate=$limit;
  server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    location /api { limit_req zone=per_tenant burst=10; proxy_pass http://api:8080; }
  }
}
```

```yaml
version: 3.8
services:
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question validates the ability to design and implement per-tenant service mesh policies in a multi-data center environment, with emphasis on dynamic policy reloads, zero-downtime updates, and strong tenant isolation.

## Key Concepts

- Consul Connect per-tenant service identities and mTLS
- Envoy sidecar injection and Traefik as an edge proxy
- Dynamic policy storage in Consul KV with hot-reload via consul-template
- Multi-data center architecture considerations and zero-downtime updates

## Code Example

```yaml
version: '3.9'
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.0
    command:
      - --providers.consulcatalog
      - --providers.consulcatalog.endpoint.address=consul:8500
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./traefik-dynamic.yml:/dynamic.yml:ro
    environment:
      - CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR=consul:8500

  consul:
    image: consul:1.17
    command: agent -server -ui -bootstrap-expect=1 -client=0.0.0.0
    ports:
      - "8500:8500"

  consul-template:
    image: hashicorp/consul-template:latest
    command: -consul-addr=consul:8500 -template "/tmp/intentions.hcl:/etc/consul-intentions/intentions.hcl:consul reload"
    volumes:
      - ./intentions.ctmpl:/tmp/intentions.hcl

  backend-tenant-a:
    image: your-backend:latest
    labels:
      - "consul.hashicorp.com/service=api-tenant-a"
      - "consul.hashicorp.com/enable-ingress-gateway=true"

  backend-tenant-b:
    image: your-backend:latest
    labels:
      - "consul.hashicorp.com/service=api-tenant-b"
```

## Bootstrap Commands

```bash
# Initialize Consul agent
consul agent -config-dir=/etc/consul.d &

# Register services with Consul
consul services register -name=api-tenant-a -id=api-tenant-a
consul services register -name=api-tenant-b -id=api-tenant-b

# Create intentions for tenant isolation
consul intention create -deny "tenant-failing" "api-tenant-a"
consul intention create -allow "tenant-permitted" "api-tenant-a"

# Enable Envoy sidecar injection
consul connect envoy -sidecar-for api-tenant-a -register &

# Reload Traefik on policy changes
consul-template -template=intentions.ctmpl -exec="traefik --reload"
```
